name: Google Review Replies + Root-Cause Tagging with Weekly Star-Loss Report

parameters.content:
## ⭐ Google Review Replies + Root-Cause Tagging

### How it works
Every new Google review gets a drafted reply and a single root-cause tag (wait time, staff, price, cleanliness and so on). Happy 4–5 star reviews with no complaint are answered automatically. Anything with a complaint goes to Slack first, so the owner approves the reply before it goes live. Every review is logged to a Google Sheet.

Every Monday the workflow reads the last 7 days from that sheet, adds up the stars lost to each fixable problem (5 minus the rating), and emails the owner one short note: the single issue that cost the most stars, plus one thing to try this week.

### Setup steps
1. Connect Google Business Profile, OpenAI, Google Sheets, Slack and Gmail credentials.
2. In **New Google Review** and **Post Reply to Google**, pick your account and location.
3. Create a sheet with these headers: `review_id, review_name, review_date, reviewer, star_rating, review_text, sentiment, root_cause, staff_mentioned, fixable, complaint_summary, draft_reply, reply_status` and select it in both Sheets nodes.
4. Replace [Business Name] and [contact email] in the reply prompt, choose a Slack channel, and set the owner's email in the Gmail node.
5. Activate the workflow.

## 📥 Review Intake
Polls Google Business Profile for new reviews, skips any that already have a reply, and turns the star value (FIVE, FOUR…) into a number.

## 🧠 Reply Draft & Root Cause
One model call writes the reply and picks one root-cause tag. The parser locks tags to a fixed list so the weekly math stays clean.

## 🗂️ Log & Route
Every review is saved to the sheet. Clean 4–5 star reviews go straight to posting; anything with a complaint waits for the owner.

## ✅ Approve & Publish
Complaint replies go to Slack with Approve / Decline buttons. Approved and auto-approved replies both end at the same Post Reply node. Declined ones stay in the sheet for a manual reply.

## 📉 Weekly Costliest-Problem Analysis
Every Monday at 9 AM, pulls the review log, keeps the last 7 days, scores each fixable tag by stars lost (5 − rating) and has the model explain the top one in plain words.

## 📧 Owner Report
Emails the weekly note straight to the owner's inbox.

## 🔐 Credentials & Security
Use OAuth2 for Google Business Profile, Sheets, Gmail and Slack, and an API key for OpenAI. Keep owner emails, sheet IDs and channel IDs out of shared copies.

values.content:
You handle Google review responses for [Business Name]. For every review you do two jobs.

JOB 1 – Draft a reply the owner can post as-is:
- Under 80 words, warm and specific to what the reviewer actually said.
- Thank them by first name.
- For complaints: apologise once, own it, and invite them to reach out at [contact email] so it can be made right.
- Never promise refunds or discounts, never argue, never name staff in a negative reply.
- No emojis, no hashtags, no copy-paste phrases like "we value your feedback".
- If there's no text (rating only), keep it to one or two sentences.

JOB 2 – Tag the root cause. Pick exactly ONE:
wait_time, staff_behavior, price, cleanliness, product_quality, booking_scheduling, communication, none, other
Use "none" when there is no complaint at all. If a staff member is named (good or bad), put their name in staff_mentioned.

Return only this JSON:
{
  "sentiment": "positive | neutral | negative",
  "root_cause": "one tag from the list",
  "staff_mentioned": "name or empty string",
  "complaint_summary": "max 12 words, empty if no complaint",
  "reply": "the reply text"
}

You write a short weekly note to a busy local business owner about their Google reviews. Focus on the ONE fixable problem that cost the most stars this week (top_problem in the data). Say how many stars it cost and across how many reviews, quote one or two of the example complaints in your own words, and suggest one concrete fix they could try this week. If a staff member shows up repeatedly, mention it neutrally. If top_problem is null, tell them it was a clean week and keep it to three sentences. Keep it under 180 words, plain and direct, no corporate tone. Use simple HTML only (

, ,

    ,
  • ). Return only this JSON: { "subject": "short email subject", "html": "the email body" }
